outcome.statement: The existing closed weighted-edge reduction exposes constant and linear source-coordinate weights, but no quadratic endpoint primitives. No RR, RZ, or ZZ closed form was obtained in this extension; all three are evaluated by one fixed tensor-Gauss triangle rule and are explicitly reported as quadrature rows.
outcome.qualification: This is an implementation result, not a proof that a higher-harmonic symbolic reduction cannot close. It establishes that the present weighted-edge-antiderivative family does not yet provide exact second-order members.

accuracy_pin.method: Conservative midpoint subdivision on the same rectangular cell at levels 6 and 7, followed by the second-order Richardson extrapolate (4 fine - coarse) / 3; errors are maximum absolute differences divided by the maximum absolute extrapolated value for each weight.
accuracy_pin.production_rule: Order-10 tensor Gauss-Legendre rule under a Duffy triangle mapping.

centroid_shift_identity.statement: A directly evaluated displaced source monopole was compared with the undisplaced value plus its source-position gradient and one-half its Hessian contraction. The gradient and Hessian columns were differentiated from the same exact traced filament kernel used for the direct evaluation.
centroid_shift_identity.verdict: pass: the residual is cubic in displacement, as required after retaining value, first moments, and second moments

cost.measurement: Median of 21 NumPy contractions after one warm evaluation; identical 256-target by 2048-cell count and float64 storage in both cases.

refinement_comparator.statement: Six fixed columns use 2.0x coupling memory and 1.982x contraction time at unchanged cell count, versus the banked refinement charge of 3.24x interaction build and 13.6x memory.

fixed_shape.statement: Three cells were evaluated together under jit(vmap); every cell retained six coefficients and agreed with the host path.
